Abstract.AbstractText: Large-scale detection of ubiquitination sites in whole cell proteomes using nanoLC-MS/MS is a well-established technique that has deepened the understanding of protein degradation processes in eukaryotic cells. Ubiquitination sites are usually identified by detection of Lys-ɛ-Gly-Gly (K-ɛ-GG)-remnant peptides, which are generated by tryptic digestion of proteomes. We show in this application note that DMSO addition to the LC mobile-phase enhances identification rates of K-ɛ-GG peptides by more than 100 % due to an increase of peptide signal intensities. The gain in the number of ubiquitination site identifications exceeds by far the gain which has been published for other post-translational modifications, namely phosphorylation and acetylation.
